Chapter 4: Into South America—New Languages, New Landscapes.
Crossing into South America, everything starts to feel different, doesn’t it? The border between Panama and Colombia is more than just a line on a map—it’s a place where the world seems to narrow, squeezed between the sea and the thick, wild jungle. Here, the trains are few and far between, their paths twisted and shaped by the land and by stories from long ago.
You can feel the sense of adventure growing stronger with every passing mile. The unknown is right there, just out of sight, pulling you forward.
Once you’re in Colombia, the train weaves its way through breathtaking mountains and quiet valleys. The jungle gradually gives way to high, open plains. The air feels heavy, humid—colors are richer, more alive. And the people? They’re warm, curious, always ready to share a story or ask about yours.
Picture meeting a university student on her way home for the holidays. She opens up about what it’s like to study in a country that’s still healing from conflict and change. But what sticks with you is her optimism—it’s contagious. Even in tough times, she’s hopeful, reminding you that hope can thrive almost anywhere.
The ride through Ecuador is all about altitude and history. Suddenly, the train is climbing into the Andes. The air grows thin and crisp. Towns cling to steep hillsides, their twisting streets full of stories. At one little station, a group of elders gathers, faces lined by years of sun and wind. They talk about the first time electricity lit up their homes, about how life has changed, and about holding onto traditions even as modern life creeps in.
Listening to them, you realize you’re catching a glimpse of a world that’s both ancient and always changing.
Traveling by train in South America? It’s a real test of patience and flexibility. Trains run late, the tracks are unpredictable, and you won’t find many comforts along the way. There are moments when it’s tough—a missed connection, a chilly night in a drafty station, or struggling to understand a new language. But then there are those magical moments that make it all worth it. Think about seeing the Andes peak above the clouds, tasting something wild and new, or hearing music drifting on the evening air through an open window.
These little moments—they’re the threads that weave the whole journey together.
In Peru, the train drops down from the mountains and glides onto the coastal plains. The landscape is stark, almost otherworldly, shaped by centuries of wind and water. Sitting across from you, a local artist is on his way to a festival. He shares how tradition runs through his art, connecting the past with the present. There’s pride in his voice—a deep love for his heritage and the stories he tells through his work.
That conversation? It’s a reminder that travel isn’t just about ticking off new destinations—it’s about finding meaning in the lives and stories of the people you meet.
As the train heads even further south, the sense of distance becomes almost overwhelming. Everything familiar slips away, replaced by a sense of wide-open possibility.
The journey through South America turns into a lesson—one about patience, resilience, and endless curiosity. You realize the world is so much bigger and more varied than you ever imagined. And maybe, the best part is discovering that every journey is shaped just as much by the people you meet as by the places you visit.
